caption: I budgeted R400 for sneakers and spent R1 800. What is your budget-versus-actual gap?

slides.title:
Where my R13 200
really went
in October
Living in Hammanskraal
slides.body:
Male, 29
Single, no kids
Job: Owns a one-chair barbershop in a container
Net income: R13 200 p/m (this month)

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: One room in a yard, shared bathroom
slides.body: I am saving to move out. The saving part is a work in progress.

slides.title: Shop costs
slides.includes: Container site fee, blades, products, a new clipper
slides.body: The clipper was R650 and it died after three weeks. I bought it again.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.body: I cook on Sundays and eat the same thing until Thursday.

slides.title: Taxi fare
slides.includes: Two taxis each way, thirty days
slides.body: The shop is the only place I go, so this one is honest.

slides.title: Sneakers
slides.body: I budgeted R400. I did not budget for the second pair. The layby made it feel smaller.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: black tax, prepaid electricity, funeral policy, barbers' stokvel, airtime & data, savings
slides.body: Six quieter items, R3 470. The stokvel is the reason I have a December at all.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R13 200. I planned on R1 800 left. This is what the October statement said instead.

slides.title: I checked
slides.body:
I uploaded October's statement to Beyond Horizon and compared it with the budget I had made.

The sneakers were four times what I planned.

No bank login needed.
